sources.title: The probable error of a mean
sources.version_consulted: Final journal scan hosted by Washington University; PDF includes one preliminary page.
sources.consulted_scope: Printed pp. 1–8: Introduction and Sections I–III, inspected visually; PDF pp. 2–9.
sources.supports: Established Gaussian small-sample mean pivot with estimated scale.
sources.does_not_support: The original argument about zero correlation alone is not a modern independence proof; the project must supply an orthogonal Gaussian-coordinate argument. Normality and independent observations remain assumptions.

sources.title: A well-conditioned estimator for large-dimensional covariance matrices
sources.version_consulted: Author-hosted publisher-typeset article-in-press PDF, displaying assigned final journal volume and pagination; every page marked ARTICLE IN PRESS.
sources.consulted_scope: Abstract, Section 1 and Section 2.1, printed pp. 365–369, Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.1, equations (4)–(9).
sources.supports: Established covariance regularisation by combining the sample covariance and an identity target; oracle quadratic-loss optimisation and the distinction from an implementable estimated weight.
sources.does_not_support: A fixed user-chosen shrinkage intensity is not the Ledoit–Wolf estimator and does not inherit its asymptotic optimality or distribution-free claims. No final-version textual identity claim.

sources.title: On estimating the expected return on the market
sources.version_consulted: NBER Working Paper 444, February 1980, On estimating the expected return on the market: an exploratory investigation. Published successor metadata verified separately; final journal body unavailable through attempted publisher retrieval.
sources.consulted_scope: Introduction, printed pp. 4–5; Appendix A, printed A1–A4, especially (A.1)–(A.5). Formula pages A1–A2 visually checked.
sources.supports: For the stipulated constant-coefficient log-return law, sample log-drift variance depends on the observation horizon, not the frequency at a fixed horizon. Finer sampling improves idealised variance estimation, subject to sampling/model limitations.
sources.does_not_support: No claim that the final published body was read, no transfer of working-paper empirical findings, no newly discovered drift-identification result, no guarantee under microstructure noise.
sources.published_status: Published peer-reviewed successor verified; only preceding working paper body consulted.

sources.title: The use of confidence or fiducial limits illustrated in the case of the binomial
sources.version_consulted: Final journal JSTOR scan hosted by Bare Statistics, with preliminary JSTOR terms page.
sources.consulted_scope: Section 1, printed pp. 404–407, especially confidence-belt construction (4)–(5).
sources.supports: Repeated-sampling binomial confidence coverage for counts from independent replication runs.
sources.does_not_support: No posterior probability interpretation for a fixed unknown parameter, no exact equality of coverage, and no joint coverage across correlated experiments. Numerical quantile calls are separate floating-point implementations.
